text:
alice_support: Hey @sparkledger_prod — saw your ticket about recurring minute-boundary 429s during bulk syncs. Can you confirm which region + model and whether this is only during your 00/15/30/45 minute jobs?

sparkledger_prod: alice_support: Thanks for picking up. It's eu-west, model: gpt-open-13b, happens around top-of-minute for a bunch of our workers. Roughly 5-10% of requests get 429s for ~60s window.

carla_cse: Quick Q: did you recently change concurrency or add new batches? Also do you use our SDK or a homegrown client?

sparkledger_prod: carla_cse: We pushed a change to rotate keys and also increased worker replicas last week. Using our own HTTP2 multiplexing client, retries are immediate (no jitter).

ben_oncall: pinging eng because immediate retries without jitter + synchronized start times = classic token/bucket alignment. @ingrid_eng can you take a look at metrics?

ingrid_eng: looking. I see a sharp correlation in the RPM short-window metric around minute-boundaries from 11:02 -> 11:03 UTC. RPM surge from ~1200 -> 4.5k for 30s then back. Rate-limit headers show X-RateLimit-RPM: 2000 and X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0 on many failed responses.

alice_support: That's useful. SparkLedger, can you paste a sample failing response headers (redact ids)? dev-bot can mask.

sparkledger_prod: dev-bot: sample headers: 
```
x-request-id: abcd-1234
x-rate-limit-rpm: 2000
x-rate-limit-tpm: 120000
x-rate-limit-remaining: 0
retry-after: 30
status: 429
```

ben_oncall: Thanks. Two quick inferences: 1) You are hitting the per-minute RPM cap (2000) during short bursts. 2) The client retry behaviour is probably amplifying the issue.

ingrid_eng: Suggestion list: 
- Capture a short tcpdump or request trace during the spike to confirm exact request timestamps.
- Check whether your token refill (if you use a local token bucket) aligns with the minute roll (many clients refill at wall-clock minutes).
- Look at our metrics: per-route short-window 5s buckets show repeated replay spikes -> suggests many parallel clients firing same job.

carla_cse: Operational mitigations we can offer: temporary quota bump for 24h, or enable short burst allowance (if you have Dedicated we can set higher RPM). Which do you prefer while we investigate?

sparkledger_prod: Prefer temporary quota bump for today to reduce user impact. Also want guidance to prevent recurrence.

alice_support: Ok, I'll open a 24-hour bump for RPM to 4000 and add a note to escalation. Expect it applied in ~15m. Meanwhile, two-prong fix: client-side and infra.

ingrid_eng: Client-side fixes (high impact): 
- Add jittered exponential backoff on 429s (example: backoff = base * 2^n * (0.5 + rand())).
- Add small random startup jitter to cron/workers so not all start exactly at :00. Even 200-500ms staggering helps a lot.
- Implement request folding: combine small concurrent requests into batched calls where possible.

ingrid_eng: Infra/Config suggestions: 
- If requests are latency-sensitive and you need headroom, consider Dedicated pool or higher RPM plan.
- Enable per-customer burst config (we can temporarily open a 60s higher ceiling).

alice_support: Also please enable the SDK header logging (or add logging of x-rate-limit-* and x-request-id) so we can match failed requests to traces. Example curl repro we often use: 
```
curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \ 
     -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ 
     -d '{"input":"test"}' \ 
     "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/models/gpt-open-13b/generate"
```

ben_oncall: For a quick repro you can run a small script that fires N parallel requests aligned to the next minute to see the fail window. Example pseudo: 
```
start = next_wall_minute()
spawn 300 workers do request at start + 10ms*worker_id
collect 429s
```

sparkledger_prod: Understood. We'll add jitter and backoff. Can you still do the 24h bump? Our SLAs are getting hit.

alice_support: Done — bumped RPM to 4000 for 24h, change id CHG-3792. Monitor dashboards for next cycle.

carla_cse: We'll follow up tomorrow w/ a postmortem and guidance doc. For now: add application-level metric to track 429_rate and time-of-day distribution, ideally percentile by minute offset.

ingrid_eng: One more note: if you use HTTP/2 connection pooling, be careful with per-connection concurrency — some clients open many streams on a single connection which can burst at reopen. Consider limiting per-connection concurrent streams and widening pool count.

ben_oncall: I'll keep an eye on the alerting for additional spikes. If the temporary bump isn't enough we'll propose an Emergency Dedicated trial.

sparkledger_prod: Thanks team. We'll deploy jitter patch in the next 40m and report back here with logs. Appreciate the fast help :thumbsup: 

dev-bot: Applied quota change CHG-3792 by alice_support. Audit link: https://console.redwood.ai/changes/CHG-3792

alice_support: Closing the loop — please ping if 429s persist after client jitter + backoff changes. We'll capture roofline perf graphs if needed. :white_check_mark:
